newsitem.title: USA: LSI Logic says inventory correction over.
newsitem.headline: LSI Logic says inventory correction over.

text.p: LSI Logic Corp's chief financial officer said it appears the semiconductor industry's year-long problem of bloated inventories has been completely corrected and order growth has resumed.

"It appears the inventory correction is over - that's what it looks like to us," Douglas Norby, chief financial officer, told the Robertson, Stephens & Co Technology conference. "We see broad-based order growth. Our backlog is increasing and we are poised for a resurgence of growth in 1997.

For LSI in particular some of the order growth will come from makers of digital video disk players, he said. LSI supplies customised semiconductor solutions, many of them for video and audio entertainment appliances like DVD players.
LSI Logic suffered a drop in sales and earnings in 1996 largely because of bloated supplies in the industry for the type of chips it makes.

Analysts expect LSI sales to start showing year-on-year growth this quarter and earnings to show year-on-year growth starting in the third quarter. Norby did not comment on sales and earnings forecasts, however.
